findings.title: Denial cache can return stale results when permissions change
findings.body: The permDenialCache is only ever written (at line 154) and never invalidated when a user's permissions change. Because the denial-cache lookup at line 117 runs before the permission cache (line 123) and the DB requery, a stale denial entry will short-circuit the request and return Allowed=false even after the user has been granted access. With shortCacheTTL = 30s, any grant that lands within 30s of an earlier deny will be ignored. Concrete scenario: user is denied → denial entry written; admin grants access via role/team within 30s; next Check returns false even though both the DB and the (refreshed) permission cache would now allow it. The denial cache needs explicit invalidation (or at minimum must be invalidated when permissions for the user change), otherwise the new "fallback to DB" path added by this PR is bypassed exactly when it is most needed.

findings.title: Denial cache key does not account for folder-tree moves
findings.body: userPermDenialCacheKey only includes the resource's direct parent folder, not the folder-tree state used by checkInheritedPermissions (service.go line 581, which walks tree.Ancestors(req.ParentFolder)). If the parent folder is later moved under an ancestor that the user does have access to, a previously-cached denial for (user, action, name, parent) will keep returning false for up to 30s even though the inherited permission check would now succeed. Example: dashboard X in folder A (user lacks access) → denial entry written; folder A is moved under folder B (user has access); user checks X → denial hit → denied. The denial cache entry should either be invalidated when folder moves happen or include a tree-version component in the key.

findings.title: Denial-cache precedence test does not actually set an allow
findings.body: In 'Should deny on explicit cache deny entry' the comment at line 981 says 'Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked', but the very next line sets the permission cache to map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}. With the value false, the cached-permission branch in Check would also have returned denied, so the test passes for the wrong reason and does not prove that the denial cache wins over an actual allow. To meaningfully exercise the precedence the cache should be set to {"dashboards:uid:dash1": true} (and ideally also assert that the permission store was never called).

findings.title: Denial cache key omits group/resource, allowing cross-API collisions
findings.body: userPermDenialCacheKey is keyed by namespace + userUID + action + name + parent, where action is derived from (group, resource, verb). Two distinct APIs that happen to translate to the same action (e.g. dashboard.grafana.app/dashboards:get and dashboard.example.com/dashboards:get both yielding dashboards:read) will share denial entries, so a denial cached for one API would incorrectly deny checks on the other for the same name+parent. The key should include the group (and ideally the resource) so that denials are scoped to the API that produced them.
